subject: Emotions
title: Sadness in Babies
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sadness in Babies.

hook.text: A six-month-old whose mother leaves the room shows genuine distress. Sadness starts before language.

buildup.text: Attachment theory says infant sadness is a survival tool. A crying baby keeps caregivers close.

discovery.text: John Bowlby mapped three stages: protest, despair, detachment. Babies cycle through grief like adults.

twist.text: Romanian orphans who never bonded showed flat affect. Without early sadness, empathy fails to develop.

climax.text: Healthy infant sadness builds the emotional circuits for love, loss, and connection later in life.

punchline.text: A baby's first cry of loss teaches the brain to love.

quiz.question: Who mapped the three stages of infant grief?
